predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: Roussillon with Vallespir, the first county, c.

successors.name: County of Barcelona
successors.text: Barcelona, Girona and Ausona, passed to Wilfred's sons

successors.name: County of Besalú
successors.text: Besalú, ceded by Wilfred to his brother Radulph in 878

successors.name: County of Roussillon
successors.text: Roussillon, Miró the Old's, passed to Sunyer II in 895

ledger.x: 795: Charlemagne establishes the Spanish March in the eastern Pyrenees.
798: Urgell and Cerdanya are added to the march.
802: 'A number of castles were established in Aragon between 798 and 802 (appointment by Count Aureolus)'; the page names no previous holder (read as stateless frontier).

820: 'with the County of Aragon following suit shortly thereafter in 820' (Spanish March page): Aragon breaks away from the march and becomes the later County of Aragon (Cliopatria's row starts in 830; the eu-12 dossier must start it in 820 or the years will differ).

826: 'After the rebellion of 826, during which Guillemó and Aissó succeeded in taking it with help from the Emirate of Córdoba' (County of Osona page); 'Osona remained depopulated and outside of Frankish control until 879'.
879: 'In 879, Wilfred the Hairy began the repopulation of the county with free minores' (County of Osona page); the Wilfred the Hairy page says Wilfred 're-created' the county in 885-886.
897: Wilfred the Hairy dies on 11 August and his holdings pass to his sons, ending the Frankish march of appointed counts.

wars.name: Frankish siege of Barcelona
wars.outcome: Louis the Pious, King of Aquitaine, took Barcelona from the wali Harun, who surrendered on 4 April 801 after a siege begun in October 800; Bera became first count.

wars.name: Frankish attempts on Huesca and Tortosa
wars.outcome: The Carolingians tried to take Tortosa and Huesca (807, 812) 'without success'; the Llobregat valley border was reinforced.

wars.name: Battle of Pancorbo
wars.outcome: The Moors defeated the Carolingians in 816.

wars.name: Revolt of Aissó and Guillemó
wars.outcome: Guillemó and Aissó took Osona 'with help from the Emirate of Córdoba' in the rebellion of 826 (Aissó is listed as ruling 826-827); the county stayed 'depopulated and outside of Frankish control until 879'.

certainty.note: The march is a loose belt of counties 'between the Pyrenees and the Ebro'; the pages date counties, not frontiers, and the southern frontier with the Upper March of al-Andalus is approximate throughout.
